title: Modulation and protection of entanglement in a two-qubit system via two interacting oscillator control
authors: Pablo Carlos López Vázquez, Andrés García, Josué Romero
abstract: We investigate the control and protection of two-qubit entanglement through engineered interactions between two auxiliary harmonic oscillators. Each qubit is coupled to a local oscillator via a dephasing interaction, while the oscillators interact through independently tunable position-position and momentum-momentum couplings. Employing the characteristic-function representation, we obtain analytical solutions for the composite-system dynamics and examine how the stability properties of the coupled oscillators determine the evolution of two-qubit concurrence. Our analysis reveals distinct dynamical regimes exhibiting entanglement revivals, suppression, or decay, and identifies configurations in which oscillator interactions effectively reduce entanglement degradation. We further investigate the influence of thermal dissipation using local and global master-equation descriptions, demonstrating that suitable oscillator couplings can preserve substantial two-qubit entanglement under the dissipative conditions considered. These results establish a connection between the dynamical stability of auxiliary bosonic modes and the controllability of entanglement in discrete-variable quantum systems, providing a potential strategy for entanglement protection through engineered oscillator interactions.
summary: This theoretical paper explores how engineered interactions between auxiliary harmonic oscillators can be used to control and protect entanglement in a two-qubit system. By analyzing the stability of the coupled bosonic modes, the authors demonstrate that specific coupling configurations can counteract entanglement decay, even when environmental dissipation is present. The methodology relies on advanced techniques like the characteristic-function representation for solving open quantum system dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates methods to control and protect entanglement in a two-qubit system by engineering interactions with auxiliary harmonic oscillators.
main_result: The study establishes a direct link between the dynamical stability of the auxiliary bosonic modes and the controllability of the two-qubit entanglement, showing that specific couplings can preserve entanglement even under dissipation.
method: The dynamics are analyzed using the characteristic-function representation to obtain analytical solutions for the composite system, covering both coherent and dissipative evolution.
model_or_system: The system consists of two qubits coupled to two interacting harmonic oscillators. The Hamiltonian includes qubit terms, oscillator terms, coupling terms, and tunable oscillator interaction terms ($\alpha \hat{x}_a \hat{x}_b +  eta \hat{p}_a \hat{p}_b$). Dissipation is modeled using both local and global master equations.
key_observables: Two-qubit concurrence (entanglement), and the dynamical stability properties (eigenvalues) of the coupled oscillators.
important_parameters: Tunable coupling strengths ($\alpha,  eta$), oscillator frequencies ($\omega_a, \omega_b$), and the ratio $\Omega = \omega_b/\omega_a$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the quadratic nature of the oscillator Hamiltonian and the use of the Born and Markov approximations for the master equation derivation.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the system setup for no dissipation, local dissipation, and global dissipation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the full Hamiltonian and system model to deriving the dynamics using the characteristic-function representation. It then analyzes the impact of different dissipation models (local vs. global) and classifies the parameter space based on oscillator stability regimes to predict entanglement evolution.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a concrete, engineered mechanism—using bosonic modes—to actively control and protect quantum information (entanglement) against environmental decoherence, a central theme in quantum information science.
